az_rad_rock.blurb: Rad Rock is a compact sport wall in the Isle of You cluster of Cochise Stronghold, standing just behind its neighbour Trad Rock in southeast Arizona. Eleven routes are on record, ten of them bolted and one set up as a top rope. This is not a beginner crag: the climbs split evenly between the 5.10 and 5.11 range, with a single 5.12 on top. The stone is generally good but can turn chossy in places, and wasps and bees sometimes nest on the face, so look before you reach. The setting is scenic, and the crag is easy to spot from the parking circle.
az_rad_rock.parking_note: Drive east from Tucson on I-10 to exit 303, then south on AZ 80 and turn onto Middlemarch Road. Follow the rough gravel for roughly ten miles to Forest Road 687, head north about two miles, and take a right to a circular parking area below the crags.

az_cochise_dome_what_s_my_line_dome.blurb: A big dome studded with chickenheads in the central Cochise Stronghold, sitting just north of the Rockfellow cluster. Most of the climbing is on its large south-facing wall. This is a multi-pitch trad destination, with lines running from two to six pitches. Eleven routes are on record: mostly trad, plus one aid line and one bolted line. The grades lean hard, with a few moderates around 5.6 and 5.8, a solid group in the 5.10s and 5.11s, and one 5.12. Its best-known line is a long, adventurous moderate. Plan a full day: the walk-in is steep from the east and longer but gentler from the west, and the views are excellent.

az_wet_beaver_crack.blurb: Wet Beaver Crack is a crack-climbing venue in the Wet Beaver Creek canyon on the Central Mogollon Rim, near the Verde Valley at about 5,000 feet. The climbing is mostly steep trad on sandstone, with one top rope among the eleven routes. Grades run from 5.8 to 5.12, and the middle of the spread sits in the 5.10s, so it suits climbers comfortable placing gear on sustained cracks. The wall is mostly east-facing and looks over a red rock swimming hole with ledges for sunning and a high diving platform. Getting there is a long trip on foot or by bike, so bring everything you need for the day.

az_submarine_steamboat_rock.blurb: A Sedona landmark and the first big rock you meet when driving in from the north, set in the Midgley Bridge area. Eleven routes are on record, mostly trad with a handful of sport lines, including a long multi-pitch bolted line. Most of the grades fall between 5.9 and 5.10, with one 5.11 and one very easy scramble-level line. It is rougher than its neighbours Tisha and Princess: expect loose rock and dirt, and treat it as an adventure rather than a polished crag. Views over Sedona from the top are wide, and the finish to the base includes a short, easy fifth-class scramble.
az_submarine_steamboat_rock.approach: From Midgley Bridge, follow Wilson Canyon Trail to the point where the Jim Thompson Trail comes in from the left. Take that trail until it nears a slickrock buttress, then leave it on a use trail climbing the buttress to the base of the rock. The last short section is easy fifth-class scrambling.

az_tasty_pancho.blurb: Tasty Pancho is a single boulder, around 15 feet tall, in the First Gully group on the San Francisco Peaks above Flagstaff in northern Arizona. Eleven bouldering problems are on record. Most fall between V3 and V6, with a couple of V8s and one V10 for the strong. Several problems begin from a crouch on the arete and the opening holds can be sharp, so pads and some care with skin are worthwhile. Other boulders in the gully, including several sectors beside this one, make it easy to build a longer session around it.

az_4_hole_show.blurb: A tight cluster of hard boulders on Middle Elden, in the Mount Elden bouldering above Flagstaff, at roughly 7,400 feet. Eleven problems are on record, and nearly all are demanding. There is a lone V2 and a V4, then a few V5s, and a run of V9 and V10 problems at the top end, so easier warm-ups are limited. The style here is powerful and crimpy, typical of Elden. The boulders sit close together on a small flat among pines, which makes moving between problems quick, and the spot gets both sun and shade. Reach it on foot via the main canyon trail.
